findings.element: state=day, "Behind you" disclosure, the "days back" measure (.b-back, data-px="2")
findings.problem: Open the disclosure on the wedding morning (the one moment this whole product is built toward) and the count column stops naming the row beside it. The past rail runs at 2px per day, so a week is 14px while a row of type is 39px tall; place() pushes only the copy clear and leaves the tick and the numeral on the true pixel. The result at every width I drove (390 and 1440 identical): 14 pairs correctly, then 28/35/42 stack as a block of three numerals beside a single title, 56/63 stack beside another, and "Final dress fitting", "Send the invitations" and "Menu tasting at The Orchard" run down the page with no numeral anywhere near them. Five of the eight rows show a figure that belongs to a different moment or no figure at all, with no leader, no bracket and nothing else joining a numeral to its row. The measure is the whole instrument of this design, and here it silently reports the wrong reading. It is invisible to both gates because the disclosure is closed at rest and every frame was shot closed.
findings.fix: In place(), when an item's computed push is greater than zero, apply the same --push to the count and its unit as to the .b-copy, so the figure travels with the words it names and the pair never breaks. Leave the tick alone on the true pixel and draw a 1px hairline in the rail's own ink from the tick across to the pushed numeral's baseline, shown only while data-crowded="true", so the reader can still see where on the measure the moment actually sits. Nothing else changes: the truth stays on the pixel, the pairing stops lying.

findings.element: state=owner-editing, the edit panel's WHEN text field and the −7/−1/+1/+7 steppers
findings.problem: The steppers sit directly under the field they appear to drive, but they never write back to it. Press −1 twice on "Send the invitations" and the row moves to Thu 6 Aug, the readout says "Thursday 6 August 2026 · in 21 days", the measure re-lays — and the field the owner is looking at still reads "8 August 2026". Two facts, one moment, in the same 300px panel. Worse, the field is now armed: focus it and press Enter without typing a character and the moment jumps back to 8 August and the two presses are gone. It is announced as "moved 1 day later", which is true of the data and false about what the person did. Every other derived fact on this surface follows the move; the one control labelled with the date does not. Nothing in the 539 assertions covers the input's own value, because they all check the row, the readout and the accessible name.
findings.fix: In the stepper handler, after committing the new date, set the WHEN input's value from the same F.fmt formatter that seeded it (skipping the write only while that input holds focus and the user has typed). In the field's Enter/commit handler, run F.parseDay on the value and return without touching the model, the history or the live region if the parsed ISO equals the moment's current date — a confirm on an unchanged field must be a no-op, not an edit.

findings.element: foot() "Updated 15 July 2026" on every surface, and "Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it" on the owner surface
findings.problem: Both strings come from the one UPDATED constant, so the surface states one field as two facts in two grammars, and neither moves. I added a moment, renamed it, moved another by a week, hid it, deleted it and undid the delete: the footer still said "Updated 15 July 2026" throughout. On the guest surfaces that stamp is the only answer to the question every guest actually has — is what I am looking at current — and it is wired to nothing. On the owner surface it also sits eight lines under "Live since 15 July", telling the owner the same date twice for two different reasons, so neither reads as load-bearing.
findings.fix: Add a changedAt to the fixture api that every mutation in wireOwner writes (add, rename, move, hide, delete, and their undos), and derive foot()'s stamp from it rather than from UPDATED; leave publication.publishedAt to carry "Live since" alone. Then pass stamp:false to foot() on the owner surface — the owner does not need to be told when they themselves last typed — and keep the stamp on phone, desk and print, where it is the guest's freshness signal and now actually is one.

findings.element: state=print, and the owner bar (Add a moment / Preview / Publish)
findings.problem: The A4 sheet is the best-composed artifact in the set and nothing in the product reaches it. Grepping every data-act in the direction gives add, preview, publish, owner, setday, copy, done, delete — there is no print. The sheet is addressed to the guest ("The plan stays online at <url>"), and the guest surfaces at phone and desk width have literally zero focusable controls, so the person it is for cannot ask for it either. A designed object with no entrance is the same as a missing state, and the brief puts the printed keepsake on the morning itself in scope.
findings.fix: Add act("Print the keepsake", false, {"data-act":"print"}) to the owner bar between Preview and Publish, wired through the existing go() to state=print with a way back on the same pattern as "Back to the plan", and add the same control to the guest header on the desk medium only (a phone cannot print, and the sheet is drawn at sheet medium). Both surfaces already force paper ground for print through forces(), so nothing else needs to change.

findings.problem: The one surface that cannot scroll and cannot be corrected once it is on the table repeats itself three times. Today's date appears twice in full ceremonial form — "79 days away on Thursday 16 July 2026" in the dateline and "Today, Thursday 16 July 2026" at the rail's origin, 200px apart. The cancelled moment appears twice — the struck-through row "City hotel shortlist / Not going ahead" and then, four lines below it, the prose "One of them did not happen." And the opening gap is stated in words ("Nothing is planned until 1 August.") beside a rail that already draws the same fortnight as visible emptiness. On screen these pairs never co-occur, because the sentence is the collapsed summary and the rows live behind the disclosure; on paper the disclosure is open by definition, so every pair prints together.
findings.fix: On the sheet medium only: drop the year and weekday from the rail origin so it reads "Today, 16 July" and lets the dateline own the ceremonial form once; suppress the behind-you summary sentence whenever the behind-you rows are themselves rendered (they always are on paper), since the struck row already carries the fact in the person's own words; and keep the gap sentence, which is the one of the three that adds a boundary date the rail does not print.

biggestWin: The measure is a real idea, not a decoration, and it survived being driven. A pixel is a unit of time on every surface, so the fortnight with nothing in it looks like a fortnight with nothing in it, and the design then pays that idea's honest cost in words rather than hiding it — "Nothing is planned until 1 August" sits pinned in a sticky column that never scrolls away, so the reader is never looking at a date without today beside it. Around that, the states nobody screenshots are the ones that are finished: the empty project asks one question, gives one example, refuses "next spring" with "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026." and keeps focus in the field; the stalled load says the plan has not been deleted and the link still works; a clipboard failure answers "Copy did not work. Select the link and copy it by hand." And the owner's editing model holds under real driving — scroll position and focus survive every repaint, resize from 1440 to 320 and back, reorder, and delete; undo is keyboard-bound, lives in one place, names what it will restore, and returns focus to the control that made the change. That is the part most products never build, and it is built here.
